page: Amazon Web Services m6gd.4xlarge is a general-purpose, ARM-based cloud instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It runs on an AWS Graviton2 processor using the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture operating at 2.5 GHz. The instance provides 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading (one thread per core). Memory capacity is configured at 64.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The hardware configuration includes a dedicated local 950 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and does not include GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier performance across multi-core compute and data-handling workloads. The instance achieves a PassMark CPU score of 9733.47 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8538.0, with stress-ng multi-core compute reaching 24287.77. In data operations, it performs well with 19.0 million Redis SET operations per second and a static web serving throughput of 18.92 GB/sec. Large uncached read bandwidth reaches 151.25 GB/sec, alongside 71.6 GB/sec large block write bandwidth.

Single-thread execution metrics highlight definite tradeoffs. Geekbench single-core performance ranks in the bottom 25% with a score of 941.0, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression falls into the bottom 10% at 7.02 GB/sec. Similarly, while medium-model LLM generation reaches average throughput at 10.71 tokens/sec, single-threaded text processing and small-model generation show low efficiency. The architecture trades off peak single-core throughput for physical core density, predictable thread isolation, and cost-efficient multi-threaded parallelism.

AWS m6gd.4xlarge is well positioned for scale-out web serving, caching clusters, relational or document database backends, and containerized microservices requiring fast local NVMe temporary storage alongside balanced memory and compute resources.
description: Amazon Web Services m6gd.4xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 16 dedicated physical ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 cores clocked at 2.5 GHz, 64.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 950 GB NVMe SSD local instance store. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor with 5 Gbps baseline networking and zero GPUs, it exhibits balanced multi-threaded performance, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 8538.0 and handling 19.0 million Redis SET operations per second. While multi-threaded throughput and uncached memory bandwidth remain steady in median tiers, single-threaded benchmarks such as Geekbench single-core (941.0) and bzip3 decompression demonstrate slower per-core execution. The physical core isolation and high local NVMe throughput make m6gd.4xlarge suitable for container clusters, microservices, key-value stores, and distributed database workloads.
